title: Usage-floor decoupling for short-burst sessions + SQ checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and validate an experiment that decouples minimum-usage floors for short-burst conversational sessions (session duration < 45s or tokens < 120) to avoid penalizing ephemeral UX (e.g., quick assistants, snippet generation). This work ties into enterprise security questionnaire requirements: produce a checklist and legal-approved wording for contract exhibits explaining floor exceptions and grace-credit behavior.
updates: 2026-02-15 Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Problem statement: customers building short-turn assistants report disproportionate floor charge where majority sessions are under 2 turns. Initial telemetry pulled (see analytics queries).

2026-02-18 Marco Nguyen: Met with Runtime eng (Sofia Chen) and Legal (Daniel Rios). Engineering flagged cache/billing side-effects for per-session classification; legal requested explicit exhibit language and audit trail for exceptions.

2026-02-24 Data team (Jamal Li): Provided distribution: median session tokens=78, 60% of sessions <120 tokens, 25% sessions <30 tokens. Proposed eligibility rule: session_duration <45s OR total_tokens <120. Attached spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/short-burst-telemetry

2026-02-28 PM review: Proposed experiment arms: A (control) existing floor; B floor waived for eligible short sessions but credits applied monthly; C floor reduced by 50% for eligible sessions. Requested cost simulation and per-customer P&L.

2026-03-03 Finance (Rina Patel): Ran Monte Carlo sim across 1k enterprise customers, expected 3-7% revenue impact on floor revenue but 12-18% reduction in customer churn risk. Simulation doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRICING/short-burst-sim

2026-03-05 Engineering design doc (PRD+API): Marco uploaded runtime gating design and billing switch with canary flagging. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/8021. Key trade-off: adding session classification increases per-request metadata and may add 1-3ms p99 latency when enabled; runtime suggests off-by-default and sampled rollout.

2026-03-08 Legal (Daniel Rios): Drafted contract exhibit language and SQ answers; requested audit logs exposing eligibility decisions and a data-retention paragraph. Draft: https://drive.google.com/contract-exhibit-short-burst

2026-03-10 Product sync: Chosen pilot = Arm B (waive floor for eligible sessions, bill monitored monthly with grace credits). Agreed acceptance criteria and telemetry events for rollback triggers. Next: build server-side flag + billing adapter, craft customer-facing FAQ, schedule legal SQ review.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot implementation deploys behind feature flag and can be enabled per-customer (dedicated toggle).
Telemetry emitted for each session: session_id, total_tokens, duration_ms, eligible_flag, billing_action (waived|reduced|full).
No >2% increase in p99 inference latency in canary region when flag is enabled (runtime verified by engineering).
Finance dashboards show projected monthly revenue delta and churn simulation for pilot cohort within expected bounds (3-9% floor revenue reduction).
Legal signs off on the exhibit wording and SQ answers; audit log retention meets enterprise customers' typical 90-day request in exhibit.
analytics_queries:
-- Median session token distribution (30d)
SELECT approx_percentile(total_tokens, 0.5) AS median_tokens, approx_percentile(total_tokens, 0.95) AS p95_tokens FROM sessions WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' AND product='hosted-api';

-- Short session rate by customer tier
SELECT customer_tier, count_if(total_tokens < 120)/count(*) as short_rate FROM sessions GROUP BY customer_tier;

-- Cost delta simulation query (join to cost per-token)
SELECT s.customer_id, sum(s.total_tokens * c.cost_per_token) as token_cost FROM sessions s JOIN cost_table c ON s.region = c.region WHERE s.created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY s.customer_id;
decision_log: 2026-03-05: Chose eligibility rule 'total_tokens <120 OR duration_ms <45000' after telemetry review; rationale: captures ephemeral UX while limiting edge cases. (PM + Data + Eng).

2026-03-06: Selected experimental arm B (full waiver) for initial pilot to maximize learnings about churn signal; will test reduced-floor in later experiment if revenue impact larger than expected. (PM + Finance).
2026-03-08: Require audit logs and SQ exhibit before enabling for enterprise customers; small customers may opt-in via self-serve toggle without exhibit. (Legal + Sales + PM).
